payload.concept: a fair test changes only one thing

plan.title: Is this a fair test of ramp height?
plan.about: A fair test changes only one thing: here only the ramp's height (1 block or 3 blocks) differs, while the car and its clay stay the same.

story.says: Two ramps, each with a red toy car at the top, side by side.
One ramp sits on 1 block, the other on 3 blocks: only the height is different.
Both cars are the same red car, and both carry the same gray ball of clay.
Both cars roll down and stop on the carpet.
Only the ramp height changed; the car and the clay are the same.

shots.intent: Both ramps ready, one above the other at one scale and square on, so the child first sees the two set-ups as a pair: ramp, blocks, car with clay.

audit.question: Can a child see two ramps, each with a red toy car waiting at the top?

shots.intent: Cut closer to the high ends, side by side at one scale and square on, so the child can count the blocks: 1 under one ramp, 3 under the other. This is the one thing that changes.

audit.question: Can a Grade 3 child count 1 block under one ramp and 3 blocks under the other?

shots.intent: Look down a little onto the two cars so their tops show: the same red car carrying the same gray lump of clay in both lanes.

audit.question: Do both red cars carry the same gray lump of clay on top?

shots.intent: One still camera for both lanes at one scale, wide enough to hold the ramps and where the cars stop: the test runs, the cars roll down and come to rest on the carpet.

audit.question: Can a child see both cars roll down their ramps and stop on the carpet?

shots.intent: For the question, cut back to the set-up, still and square on, one scale: the 1 block and 3 blocks labelled, and the same car with the same clay on each. A fair test is judged by its set-up.

audit.question: Can a Grade 3 child see that only the number of blocks is different, while the car and the clay are the same in both?

plan.notes: The question is about the set-up (is the test fair?), so the paused frame cuts back to the start: by pause:result the cars are far down the carpet (0.8 m and 1.4 m) and the blocks alone would not show that the car and clay are the same. The split rows are 32:9 bands, so set-up shots use a 1.0 m window to fit the 0.25 m tall high ramp. The close-ups use columns, so the blocks and clay are big. The recognizer lists clay as a variable in the bottom run only because its position and box change with the steeper tilt (7.9 x 2 cm vs 7.7 x 2.9 cm). It is the same gray clay in both, and the plan labels it as the same.
